questions.a: The sieve is DETERMINISTIC PYTHON ONLY. The LLM is in the parameter-adjustment loop, never in the measurement path.
This is the learns-its-gates founding intention made concrete for one gate shape.
Hex is the inference target (the M1 Studio box), not CC. CC is too expensive for periodic review.
The schedule fires from a probe — an event that already fires (the heartbeat, or a feedback-count threshold) — never a new timer or daemon.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [FIXME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(gate-parameters-adjust-from-feedback) -> PROVED

watchme.trigger: a scheduled LLM inspection completes and produces feedback on gate calibration
watchme.enough: three inspection cycles where the feedback led to a parameter adjustment, or Akien rules the initial calibration stable
watchme.carrier: the before/after gate parameter values and the feedback that prompted the change
watchme.consumer: Akien at triage — the inspection cycle must demonstrably tune the gates, not merely confirm them

dependencies: cairn/tools/feedback — the tool that owns the feedback route and the shape of a declared route. This ticket consumes what it produces.
inference_domain — the sole path to Hex (the M1 Studio inference box). The LLM prompt goes through this domain and no other.
A gate that already collects data in a structured shape — at least one sieve must be producing feedback records before this can fire against real data.

RULED 2026-08-21 (2026-08-21-feedback-is-probes-two-consumer-kinds): this ticket is the CONSUMPTION side of the passive consumer case. An inspector receives feedback to a data-recorder tool (ticket feedback-data-recorder); this ticket's LLM inspection reads from that recorder and proposes parameter adjustments. The data recorder is the 'gate that already collects data in a structured shape' named above.
filed_edges: The same feedback-review pattern applies to EVERY gate with parameters, not just sieves. This ticket builds it for one shape; the pattern transfers on the shape of the gate, not the identity of the sieve.
The adjustment record is itself a measurement (Law 10) and belongs in the gate's own history — not in a separate store.
